name: Kenvue
industry: consumer health and personal care brands
desc: Consumer health company owning Neutrogena, Listerine, Tylenol, Band-Aid, Aveeno, Johnson's Baby and Zyrtec brands, sold worldwide.
ownership: subsidiary of Kimberly-Clark (acquisition completed Nov 2026; Kenvue delisted from NYSE)
capacity_detail: Acquired by Kimberly-Clark for USD 48.7bn enterprise value, completed November 2026 (also revenue USD 15.1bn in 2025)
markets: Area served worldwide; brands include Neutrogena, Listerine, Tylenol, Calpol, Le Petit Marseillais, Nicorette and Zyrtec across many countries.
rationale: Mass consumer health brands like Neutrogena and Listerine need global reach; F1's audience growth in the US suits a newly combined Kimberly-Clark portfolio.

name: InPost
desc: Parcel locker and delivery company running over 20,000 lockers across Poland, the UK, France, Italy, Iberia and Benelux.
ownership: private: consortium of Advent International 37%, FedEx 37%, A&R 16%, PPF 10% (take-private completed Nov 2026)
capacity_detail: Acquired by a FedEx and Advent International-led consortium for EUR 7.8bn, completion reported 23 November 2026
sponsorships: Poland national football team (since 2022); Newcastle United official sponsor (2023); Atlético Madrid logistics sponsor (Aug 2024); Tour de France partner via Mondial Relay (2023)
markets: Poland, Italy, the UK, France, Benelux, Spain and Portugal; over 20,000 lockers and 18,000 pick-up/drop-off points.
rationale: Consumer-facing delivery brand already buying Premier League and La Liga deals; F1 would extend its pan-European visibility under new owners.

name: Theramex
desc: Specialty pharma company selling women's health treatments for menopause, fertility, contraception and osteoporosis in over 80 countries.
ownership: private equity: Carlyle and PAI Partners, agreed sale to Cinven (Nov 2026)
capacity_detail: Cinven agreed to acquire Theramex for about EUR 2.6bn from Carlyle and PAI Partners (Nov 2026)
markets: More than 80 countries across Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin America; menopause, fertility, contraception and osteoporosis therapies.
rationale: Women's health brand under new Cinven ownership; F1's growing female audience offers awareness, though pharma promotion rules limit consumer marketing.

name: Flint Group
desc: Home services group running 20 regional HVAC, plumbing and electrical brands across 15 US states.
ownership: private equity: General Atlantic, majority stake being sold to Permira (Nov 2026)
capacity_detail: Permira agreed to buy a majority stake from General Atlantic in a deal valued at more than USD 1.5bn (Nov 2026)
markets: United States: 20 brands in 15 states, grown from seven regional brands in five states since 2023.
rationale: Fast-growing US home-services roll-up; a US Grand Prix or team tie-in could unify local brands, but its domestic focus limits fit.

name: PGP Glass
desc: Glass packaging maker supplying bottles for pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, cosmetics and perfumery from India, Sri Lanka and the US.
ownership: private equity: Blackstone, agreed sale to Brookfield (Nov 2026)
capacity_detail: Brookfield to buy PGP Glass from Blackstone for USD 1.7bn (reported 23 Nov 2026); revenue about INR 4,000 crore (USD 430M) in FY24
markets: Plants in India, Sri Lanka and the US; markets include India, Brazil and the UK; customers include Diageo and Pernod Ricard.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier to spirits and perfume brands; F1 hospitality could reach luxury-brand customers, but consumer visibility is low.

name: Cary Group
desc: Vehicle glass repair and replacement group with about 1,800 workshops in 13 European countries.
ownership: private equity: Nordic Capital (CVC exiting); CPP Investments and Ontario Teachers' to join as equal co-owners
capacity_detail: Net revenue SEK 9bn in the 12 months to October 2026 (approx. USD 850M); OTPP to invest EUR 545m and CPP EUR 500m
markets: 13 European countries with a Nordic focus; about 1,800 workshops, 4,500 employees and 1.4 million glass jobs a year.
rationale: Car-owner service brand across Europe; motorsport sponsorship fits automotive aftermarket rivals and could support its multi-country brand building.

name: Pizza Hut
desc: Pizza restaurant chain with an estimated 15,600 locations in over 100 countries, carved out of Yum! Brands.
ownership: private equity: LongRange Capital (worldwide except Mainland China; carve-out from Yum! Brands completed Sep 2026)
capacity_detail: Yum! Brands sold Pizza Hut (excluding Mainland China) to LongRange Capital for USD 1.5bn, completed September 2026
sponsorships: Official pizza sponsor of the NFL (Feb 2018); official QSR of the Supercars Championship (Mar 2022)
markets: Estimated 15,600 locations in more than 100 countries, including the US, Canada, Mexico, the UK, Asia and Australia.
rationale: Global fast-food brand now independent under private equity; peers use F1 for youth reach, and it already sponsors NFL and Supercars.

name: Infinity Transportation
desc: Full-service lessor of rail and intermodal equipment, being sold by KKR to Ares Management.
ownership: private equity: KKR, agreed sale to Ares Management (Oct 2026)
capacity_detail: Ares Management to acquire Infinity Transportation from KKR for USD 2.9bn (Oct 2026)
markets: Rail and intermodal equipment leasing; the deal page names no countries.
rationale: Asset-heavy B2B lessor with little consumer profile; F1 hospitality might serve customer entertainment, but fit is weak.

name: Canaccord Genuity Wealth Management (UK & Crown Dependencies)
desc: Wealth management business of Canaccord Genuity in the UK and Crown Dependencies, being sold to Centerbridge and Mubadala.
ownership: subsidiary of Canaccord Genuity Group; agreed sale to Centerbridge Partners and Mubadala (Nov 2026)
capacity_detail: Centerbridge Partners and Mubadala agreed to acquire it for GBP 1.17bn (about USD 1.55bn), Nov 2026
markets: Wealth management clients in the United Kingdom and the Crown Dependencies, per the deal announcement.
rationale: Wealth manager targeting affluent clients; F1 hospitality and brand fit high-net-worth audiences as it becomes a stand-alone firm.
